definition: A quantitative-reasoning maths benchmark used in this archive almost exclusively as an out-of-domain evaluation: papers train on MATH500, AMC or AIME data and report Minerva alongside GPQA-Diamond and OlympiadBench to show the method did not overfit its training distribution. The sources use the name for the benchmark rather than for the model it was introduced with. Because it is always in the held-out group, no source here characterises its difficulty or size directly.

evidence.note: Uses integrated-gradient token attribution, aggregated into per-segment strength and direction-consistency scores, to pick which segments of a long chain-of-thought an SFT run should compute loss on, masking the rest.
evidence.title: Segment-Level Attribution for Selective Learning of Long Reasoning Traces

evidence.note: AutoThink uses a three-stage RL curriculum with stage-wise reward shaping to teach R1-style distilled models to decide per problem whether to emit an explicit reasoning chain at all.
evidence.title: Learning When to Think: Shaping Adaptive Reasoning in R1-Style Models via Multi-Stage RL

evidence.note: DiffAdapt trains a small probe on a reasoning model's hidden state to classify each question as Easy/Normal/Hard and picks a matching prompt, temperature and token limit, cutting token use without retraining the model.
evidence.title: DiffAdapt: Difficulty-Adaptive Reasoning for Token-Efficient LLM Inference

evidence.note: Defines an empirical accuracy-vs-token-budget frontier for a fixed base reasoning model, measures how far existing efficiency methods fall short of it with a single metric (REG), and proposes REO-RL, an RL objective that targets a handful of token budgets to close most of that gap.
evidence.title: How Far Are We from Optimal Reasoning Efficiency?

evidence.note: Ada-R1 merges a long-CoT and a short-CoT model into one hybrid, then applies two levels of preference training so the model first picks a reasoning style per problem and then prefers the shorter correct trace within that style, cutting average reasoning length by about 51% on five maths datasets.
evidence.title: Ada-R1: Hybrid-CoT via Bi-Level Adaptive Reasoning Optimization

evidence.note: Trains Qwen3-8B to split its chain of thought into concurrently decoded threads that spawn and join, so the critical path is shorter than a sequential trace of the same total length, using a trie-based rollout that runs on stock autoregressive inference engines.
evidence.title: ThreadWeaver: Adaptive Threading for Efficient Parallel Reasoning in Language Models

evidence.note: FROST uses attention weights to identify and prune sentence-level 'reasoning outliers' from a reasoning model's chain of thought, reporting an average 69.68% token reduction and 26.70% accuracy gain over the base model on four maths benchmarks.
evidence.title: FROST: Filtering Reasoning Outliers with Attention for Efficient Reasoning

evidence.note: QFFT fine-tunes a short-CoT instruct model on Long CoT responses with the question deleted from every training example, so the model keeps its default concise reasoning and switches to reflective Long CoT only when it hits uncertainty or an error, cutting average tokens by roughly 50% at accuracy comparable to ordinary SFT.
evidence.title: QFFT, Question-Free Fine-Tuning for Adaptive Reasoning

name: Minerva
